newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-VELEZ, RACING PLAY TWICE IN SAME DAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VELEZ, RACING PLAY TWICE IN SAME DAY.

text.p: Velez Sarsfield and Racing Club of Argentina were involved in a bizarre case of fixture congestion on Sunday as they each played two official games in two different countries on the same day.
The two clubs played each other in an Argentine championship match in Buenos Aires but also took part in Libertadores Cup matches away to different Ecuadorean oppoents.

Despite the furore which surrounded this week's announcement of the birth of Dolly the cloned sheep in Britain, the two coaches may have longed for the chance to clone their teams as they faced two fixtures within a few hours of each other at venues thousands of kilometres apart.
Velez coach Oswaldo Piazza opted to send his first team to Ecuador where they played in Guayaquil against Emelec.

Racing Club coach Alfio Basile put his priority on the Argentine championship, fielding a stronger side against Velez in Buenos Aires and throwing reserve and youth team players into the fray against Nacional in Quito.
Racing, who have not won the Argentine title for 31 years, came out top in the domestic game as they beat Velez's reserves 2-1 to claim their first win of the current championship.

But they lost 2-0 to Nacional in Quito, a result which left them bottom of Libertadores Cup group two and in danger of not making the second round. Velez, on the other hand, beat Emelec 3-2 to go second in the same group.
Fixture congestion has become a hallmark of Latin American soccer, where there is a multitude of competitions organised at continental, national and -- in Brazil -- even regional level.
Coaches are often forced to take calculated risks by fielding reserve teams against opponents where they think they can get away with it.
Mexico played a crucial World Cup qualifying soccer match on Sunday -- while the country's national championship continued unabated with six games taking place almost immediately afterwards.
Last month, the problem again reached absurd proportions as Brazilian club Cruzeiro played two matches in one night at their stadium in Belo Horizonte.
